description: A safety officer must decide whether to reopen a forklift battery-charging bay after a hydrogen alarm and establish the overnight charging controls, with input from facilities maintenance and environmental health and safety.

shared_context.S1: Forklift battery-charging Bay 4 sounded a hydrogen alarm during the afternoon shift.
shared_context.S2: The alarm has reset, there is no visible damage in the bay, and overnight production needs charging capacity for six forklifts.
shared_context.S3: Bay 2 is an available charging area that is normally reserved for maintenance vehicles, and Nora can authorize its temporary use.
shared_context.S4: The site's incident-closeout routine uses a round-robin check: Nora must give the facilities maintenance lead and the EHS specialist each a designated report-entry turn, receive both formal reports, read back the operating plan, and assign follow-up actions before authorizing charging. If a report is not entered on its first turn, Nora gives that person another report-entry turn before the closeout can be completed.
shared_context.S5: For this closeout routine, assigning follow-up actions is sufficient; Nora does not wait for maintenance work orders, incident attachments, repairs, or tests to be completed during the meeting.

PF1.text: Eli inspected Bay 4 after the alarm and found that its exhaust-fan belt has failed; the replacement belt is on site, but fitting and testing it will take exactly 6 hours. He has not entered the emergency work order yet because the maintenance system was offline during the inspection.

PF2.text: Priya's same-day EHS review found that the alarm was caused by hydrogen accumulation and that Bay 2 is approved for no more than 4 simultaneous forklift chargers; the charging policy requires a 2-hour fire watch and a gas test showing less than 1% hydrogen before any charging resumes. She has not attached the review to the incident record because the shift handover is still open.

acceptance_conditions: Bay 4 must remain closed or offline for charging until its failed exhaust fan is repaired and tested.
The Bay 4 repair must be scheduled for exactly 6 hours.
A ventilation test must occur before charging resumes.
Temporary Bay 2 use must be limited to exactly 4 simultaneous forklift chargers.
A 2-hour fire watch must be assigned before charging resumes.
The gas-test requirement must be recorded as less than 1% hydrogen.
The emergency exhaust-fan repair work order must be assigned as a follow-up action or recorded as logged.
The EHS review must be assigned for recording as a follow-up action or recorded as attached.
The final plan must cite both the maintenance finding and the EHS finding.

content_checks.C7: decisions['repair_work_order_logged'] == True or any(('work order' in c.get('detail', '')) and ('Eli' in c.get('target', '')) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: decisions['ehs_review_recorded'] == True or any(('EHS review' in c.get('detail', '')) and ('Priya' in c.get('target', '')) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The failed exhaust-fan belt changes Bay 4 charging from allowed to prohibited, sets the repair duration to exactly 6 hours, requires a ventilation test, and requires Eli's work-order follow-up to be assigned or logged.

The EHS review changes the temporary plan to exactly 4 Bay 2 chargers, sets a 2-hour fire watch, fixes the gas-test requirement as less than 1% hydrogen, and requires Priya's EHS-review follow-up to be assigned or recorded.
